newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-ITALY UPSET FRANCE, DREAM OF FIVE NATIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ITALY UPSET FRANCE, DREAM OF FIVE NATIONS.

text.p: Italy beat France for the first time in 70 years of trying on Saturday, their upset 40-32 victory over the grand slam champions boosting their Five Nations aspirations.

The Italians, who fell behind by three points only once in the match, ran in four tries against a French team that included only half the side that clinched France's fifth grand slam by beating Scotland in Paris a week ago.
The place kicking of Italy's Argentine-born fly-half Diego Diminguez, who notched up half his side's points by converting all four of his team's tries and four penalties, made the difference.
France also scored four tries, two by centre Pierre Bondouy whose last-minute second touchdown made it a more respectable final scoreline for the hosts after they had gone 40-20 behind.

"We showed great will," said Italy's French coach Georges Coste. "We have been wanting to get into the (Five Nations) tournament for a long time and I've always told my players that only the results on the field will allow us to merit the invitation."

The Italians' adventure against the makeshift French side was rewarded quickly when veteran centre Ivan Francescato went over for the first try after six minutes, taking a pass from scrum-half Alessandro Troncon following a ruck.

France replied with a penalty try, also converted by fly-half David Aucagne, to draw level, but the only time the hosts were in front was when Aucagne put them 13-10 up with his second successful penalty 25 minutes into the game.
Italy changed ends ahead after Australian-born flanker Julian Gardner scored their second try, forcing his way over from a scrum near the line.
The fast Bondouy, in his first full international, put the teams level with his first try on the hour.
But the Italians, despite playing against the wind in the second half, ran the ball in exciting handling movements they have learnt from the French over the years.

The best of these led to lock Giambattista Croci's try, then after two more Dominguez penalties, wing Paolo Vaccari was put over by Gardner after the flanker had cut through a lax French defence from inside his own half.
France came back against the tiring Italians with the late tries by full-back Jean-Luc Sadourny and Bondouy, but ran out of time to save the match.
"We were beaten by an Italian side who imposed their game," France's assistant coach Pierre Villepreux said.
"I'm disappointed because we didn't play and looked hesitant and tired. But that puts our feet back on the ground," he added as France now look ahead to touring Australia in June.
"The Italians were hungrier. We were under a lot of pressure and lost the ball too often," said wing and former captain Philippe Saint-Andre, back after a long injury layoff.

France - 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Stephane Ougier, 13-Yann Delaigue, 12-Pierre Bondouy, 11-Philippe Saint-Andre; 10-David Aucagne, 9-Guy Accoceberry; 8-Fabien Pelous (captain), 7-Philippe Benetton, 6-Arnaud Costes (replacement: 19-Serge Betsen), 5-Hugues Miorin, 4-Olivier Merle, 3-Franck Tournaire, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Marc de Rougemont.

Italy - 15-Javier Pertile; 14-Paolo Vaccari, 13-Stefano Bordon, 12-Ivan Francescato (replacement: 20-Francesco Mazzariol), 11-Marcello Cuttita; 10-Diego Dominguez, 9-Alessandro Trocon; 8-Julian Gardner, 7-Andrea Sgorlon, 6-Massimo Giovanelli (captain), 5-Walter Cristofoletto, 4-Giambattista Croci, 3-Franco Properzi, 2-Carlo Orlandi, 1-Massimo Cuttita.
